title: Thread Lifecycle and Interruption
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of thread lifecycle and interruption and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—thread states—in a small, readable example.
Identify one failure, compatibility, security, or resource-management concern and describe a safe response.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study thread lifecycle and interruption with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you coordinate tasks without depending on unpredictable scheduling or shared mutable state. In this lesson, focus on thread states and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Concurrency introduces shared-state ordering and cancellation concerns. Prefer task abstractions and immutable data where possible, coordinate access explicitly, and always define shutdown, timeout, and failure behavior. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect thread states with sleeping and joining before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.title: Thread states
items.text: Concurrency introduces shared-state ordering and cancellation concerns. Prefer task abstractions and immutable data where possible, coordinate access explicitly, and always define shutdown, timeout, and failure behavior.

items.title: Sleeping and joining
items.text: Concurrency creates ordering, cancellation, and shared-state concerns. Define task lifetime, synchronization and shutdown behavior; never rely on thread scheduling to produce a particular print order. Apply that reasoning specifically to sleeping and joining and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming one timing or memory observation proves a performance conclusion.
common_mistakes.why: JIT warm-up, scheduling, allocation, and workload changes can distort single measurements.
common_mistakes.fix: Use repeatable workloads and appropriate JDK diagnostics, and record the environment.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing only a single happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Boundary values and failures often reveal assumptions hidden by the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add an empty, boundary, or invalid case and state the expected behavior before running it.

common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify the actual cause of a different result.
common_mistakes.fix: Change one factor at a time and keep a short record of observed behavior.
